verdict.rationale: ROS 2 ships official client libraries in several languages, and the docs confirm working C++ and Python APIs, an idiomatic Python interface, and a Python rosbag API. However, the docs say several core features (intra-process communication, composition, managed lifecycles, content filtering) are 'currently only in C++', so the SDKs are not at parity across languages. missing for 10: feature parity across the official SDKs (several core features are C++-only), an enumerated list of supported languages with API reference depth, and independent hands-on corroboration of the SDK developer experience.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: Client libraries come in a variety of programming languages so that users may write ROS 2 code in the language that is best-suited for their application.
client libraries expose to users the core functionality that makes ROS "ROS"
This verifies both the C++ and Python APIs are working properly.
The interface provides an idiomatic Python experience that uses native Python types and patterns like lists and context objects.
It also provides a Python API for reading from and writing to a bag from your own source code.
Inter- and intra-process communication using the same API - Currently only in C++.
